title: A vanishing cohomology group of a pseudo-coherent complex at a prime cuts the localized complex into an upper and a lower part
author: The Stacks Project Authors
work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra)
source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-algebra.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
difficulty_reason: The lemma takes a ring R, a prime p, an integer i, and a pseudo-coherent complex K^bullet with H^i(K^bullet tensor^L kappa(p)) = 0, and asserts the existence of f not in p and a canonical direct sum decomposition of the localized complex into the truncations tau_{>= i+1} and tau_{<= i-1}, with the upper part perfect and of tor-amplitude in [i+1, infinity] (source lines 19866-19881). The proof, as the author notes, is a direct one rather than a citation: it reduces to a bounded above complex of finite free modules, inspects degree i, and writes the differentials there as matrices A and B (proof lines 19887-19895). The vanishing hypothesis is then unwound into the statement that A mod p has rank r and B mod p has rank m - r, which yields an r x r minor a of A and an (m - r) x (m - r) minor b of B both outside p (proof lines 19896-19899). Setting f = ab, the proof exhibits explicit summand decompositions of K^{i-1}, K^i and K^{i+1} after inverting f such that the two differentials kill off complementary summands and are isomorphisms on the others, so that K^bullet becomes quasi-isomorphic to the displayed two-piece complex (proof lines 19900-19914). The non-routine content is the extraction of the two minors from the rank statement and the explicit reblocking of the three free modules.
